title: Celsus confuses Christians with the Ophites
source_text: Ἑξῆς δὲ τοῖς ἐξετασθεῖσιν ὁ Κέλσος ὡς πρὸς πάντας Χριστιανοὺς ἀποτείνει λόγον, ὅντινα πρὸς τοὺς πάντῃ ἀλλοτρίους τῆς Ἰησοῦ διδασκαλίας ὁμολογοῦντας εἶναι εἰ ἄρα λέγειν ἥρμοζεν. Ὀφιανοὶ γὰρ, ὡς καὶ ἐν τοῖς ἀνωτέρω ἐλέγομεν, τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐξ ὅλων ἀρνούμενοι ἢ εἴ τινες ἄλλοι τὰ παραπλήσια ἐκείνοις φρονοῦντές εἰσιν οἱ τὰ εἴδωλα προμνώμενοι, πλάνοι καὶ γόητες· καὶ ἐκεῖνοί εἰσιν οἱ τὰ ὀνόματα τῶν θυρωρῶν ἀθλίως ἐκμανθάνοντες. μάτην οὖν πρὸς Χριστιανούς φησι τό· κἂν ἡγεμόνα τῆς ὁδοῦ ταύτης ζητῆτε, φευκτέοι μὲν ὑμῖν οἱ πλάνοι καὶ γόητες καὶ τὰ εἴδωλα προμνώμενοι. καὶ μηδ᾿ ἐπιστάμενος ὅτι οἱ τοιοῦτοι οὐκ ἔλαττον Κέλσου ὡς γόητες σὺν ἐκείνῳ κακῶς λέγουσι τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν κατ᾿ αὐτὸν θεοσέβειαν, φησὶ φύρων ἡμᾶς ἐν ἐκείνοις τῷ ἑαυτοῦ λόγῳ· ἵνα μὴ παντάπασιν ἦτε καταγέλαστοι, τοὺς μὲν ἄλλους, τοὺς δεικνυμένους θεοὺς, ὡς εἴδωλα βλασφημοῦντες τὸν δὲ καὶ αὐτῶν ὡς ἀληθῶς εἰδώλων ἀθλιώτερον καὶ μηδὲ εἴδωλον ἔτι ἀλλ᾿ ὄντως νεκρον σέβοντες καὶ πατέρα ὅμοιον αὐτῷ ζητοῦντες. ὅτι γὰρ μὴ ἐπιστάμενος, τί μὲν Χριστιανοὶ λέγουσι τί δὲ οἱ τοιούτους μύθους ἀναπλάσσοντες, ἀλλ᾿ οἰόμενος ἡμῖν προσεῖναι τὰ ἐκείνοις προσαγόμενα ἐγκλήματα ταῦτα λέγει πρὸς ἡμᾶς οὐ προσόντα ἡμῖν, δῆλον ἐκ τοῦ· τὴν μὲν δὴ τοιάνδε ἀπάτην καὶ τοὺς θαυμαστοὺς ἐκείνους συμβούλους καὶ τὰ δαιμόνια ῥήματα, τὰ πρὸς τὸν λέοντα καὶ τὸν ἀμφίβιον καὶ τὸν ὀνοειδῆ καὶ τοὺς ἄλλους καὶ τοὺς θεσπεσίους θυρωροὺς, ὧν τὰ ὀνόματα ἀθλίως ἐκμανθάνοντες οἱ δύστηνοι κακῶς δαιμονᾶτε καὶ ἀνασκολοπίζεσθε. καὶ οὐκ εἶδέ γε ὅτι οὐδεὶς τῶν τὸν λεοντοειδῆ καὶ τὸν ὀνοειδῆ καὶ τὸν ἀμφίβιον νομιζόντων εἶναι θυρωροὺς τῆς ἀνόδου ἕως θανάτου ἵσταται κἂν ὑπὲρ τῆς φαινομένης αὐτῷ ἀληθείας. ἀλλὰ τὸ ὑφ᾿ ἡμῶν δι᾿ εὐσεβείας, ἵν᾿ οὕτως εἴπω, ὑπερβολὴν γινόμενον, παρεχόντων ἑαυτοὺς παντὶ τρόπῳ θανάτου, καὶ τὸ ἀνασκολοπίζεσθαι ἐκείνοις προσάγει τοῖς μηδὲν τούτων πάσχουσιν· καὶ ἡμῖν τοῖς ἀνασκολοπιζομένοις δι᾿ εὐσέβειαν ὀνειδίζει τὴν ἐκείνων περὶ τὸν λεοντοειδῆ καὶ τὸν ἀμφίβιον καὶ τὰ λοιπὰ μυθοποιΐαν οὐ διὰ Κέλσον τοίνυν φεύγομεν τὸν περὶ λεοντοειδοῦς καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν λόγον, οὐδὲ γὰρ τὴν ἀρχὴν τοιοῦτόν τι παρειλήφαμεν· ἀλλ᾿ ἀκολουθοῦντες τῇ διδασκαλίᾳ Ἰησοῦ τὰ ἐναντία ἐκείνοις λέγομεν, οὐ συγκατατιθέμενοι τῷ τοιόνδε εἶναι τῷ προσώπῳ τὸν Μιχαὴλ καὶ τοιόνδε ἕτερόν τινα τῶν προκατειλεγμένων.
pass_a_gloss: Next (ἑξῆς) after the things examined (ἐξετάζω) Celsus as to all Christians stretches out (ἀποτείνω) a speech (λόγος), which, if it were fitting (ἁρμόζω) to say at all, [should be said] to those confessing (ὁμολογέω) themselves to be wholly foreign (ἀλλότριος) to the teaching (διδασκαλία) of Jesus. For the Ophians (Ὀφιανοί), as we said above, denying (ἀρνέομαι) Jesus entirely, or any others thinking (φρονέω) similar things to them, are those who act as go-betweens for / procure (προμνάομαι) idols/phantoms (εἴδωλα), deceivers (πλάνος) and sorcerers (γόης); and those are the ones wretchedly (ἀθλίως) learning by heart (ἐκμανθάνω) the names of the doorkeepers (θυρωρός). In vain (μάτην) then he says to Christians: "And if you seek a guide (ἡγεμών) of this road (ὁδός), you must flee (φευκτέος) the deceivers and sorcerers and those procuring idols." And not even knowing that such men, no less than Celsus, as sorcerers, along with him speak evil (κακῶς λέγω) of Jesus and of all the worship of God (θεοσέβεια) according to him, he says, mixing (φύρω) us with them in his own argument: "so that you may not be altogether laughable (καταγέλαστος), blaspheming (βλασφημέω) the others, the gods being shown (δείκνυμι), as idols, but revering (σέβω) one more wretched (ἀθλιώτερος) even than them, truly idols, and no longer even an idol but really a corpse (νεκρός), and seeking a father like him." For that not knowing what Christians say and what those fabricating (ἀναπλάσσω) such myths (μῦθος), but supposing the charges (ἔγκλημα) brought against them to belong to us, he says these things to us not belonging to us, is clear from: "Such deceit (ἀπάτη) and those wonderful counsellors (σύμβουλος) and the demonic (δαιμόνιος) words, those to the lion and the amphibious one (ἀμφίβιος) and the ass-shaped one (ὀνοειδής) and the others, and the divine/marvellous (θεσπέσιος) doorkeepers, whose names you wretches (δύστηνος) wretchedly learn, are evilly demon-possessed (δαιμονάω) and are impaled (ἀνασκολοπίζω)." And he did not see that none of those believing the lion-shaped (λεοντοειδής) and the ass-shaped and the amphibious to be doorkeepers of the ascent (ἄνοδος) stands (ἵσταμαι) until death even for the truth appearing to him. But what comes about from us on account of (διά + acc.) the excess (ὑπερβολή), so to speak, of piety (εὐσέβεια), offering ourselves to every manner (τρόπος) of death, and the being impaled, he applies (προσάγω) to those suffering none of these; and to us being impaled for piety he reproaches (ὀνειδίζω) their myth-making (μυθοποιΐα) about the lion-shaped and the amphibious and the rest. Not because of Celsus then do we flee the account about the lion-shaped and the rest, for we did not even at the beginning receive (παραλαμβάνω) any such thing; but following (ἀκολουθέω) the teaching of Jesus we say the opposite to them, not assenting (συγκατατίθεμαι) that Michael is such in face (πρόσωπον), and such some other of those listed before (προκαταλέγω).
pass_b_english: After the passages we have examined, Celsus directs a speech as though to all Christians. If it was fitting to say it at all, it should have been said to those who admit that they are wholly foreign to the teaching of Jesus. For the Ophites, as we said earlier, who deny Jesus outright, or any others who think as they do, are the ones who traffic in idols, the deceivers and sorcerers; and they are the ones who wretchedly learn by heart the names of the doorkeepers. It is idle, then, for him to say to Christians: “And if you seek a guide for this road, you must shun the deceivers and sorcerers and those who traffic in idols.”

He does not even know that such men, sorcerers as they are, speak evil of Jesus and of all the worship of God that he taught, no less than Celsus does and together with him. Mixing us up with them in his own argument, he says: “so that you may not be utterly ridiculous, blaspheming the others, the gods that are displayed, as idols, while you revere one who is more wretched even than what are truly idols, and no longer even an idol but really a corpse, and seek a father like him.”

For that he does not know what Christians say and what is said by those who invent such myths, but supposes that the charges brought against them belong to us, and so says to us things that do not apply to us, is plain from these words: “This kind of deceit, then, and those wonderful counsellors, and the demonic words addressed to the lion, and to the amphibious one, and to the ass-shaped one, and to the others, and the marvellous doorkeepers, whose names you poor wretches learn by heart to your misery, and are grievously possessed and impaled.”

He did not see that none of those who believe that the lion-shaped, the ass-shaped and the amphibious one are doorkeepers of the ascent stands firm to the point of death, even for what seems to him to be the truth. But what we do from an excess of piety, if I may put it so, when we offer ourselves to every kind of death, and being impaled as well, he attaches to those who suffer none of these things; and to us, who are impaled for the sake of piety, he makes a reproach of their myth-making about the lion-shaped one, the amphibious one and the rest. It is not, then, because of Celsus that we shun the teaching about the lion-shaped one and the rest, for we never received any such thing to begin with. Rather, following the teaching of Jesus, we say the opposite of what they say, and we do not accept that Michael has a face of this sort, or some other of those listed earlier a face of that sort.

choices.choice: Ὀφιανοί rendered “Ophites”, the usual English name; Origen describes their diagram and the animal-faced archons (Michael as lion-shaped) earlier in Book 6 (6.24-38, esp. 6.30), hence “as we said earlier”. τὰ εἴδωλα προμνώμενοι: προμνάομαι is “woo/court on another’s behalf, procure”; rendered “traffic in idols”. εἴδωλα may also carry the sense “phantoms”, but Celsus’s next sentence plays on “idols”, so “idols” is kept throughout. τοὺς δεικνυμένους θεούς: “the gods that are shown to you” (the visible gods / cult images pointed out). ὡς γόητες σὺν ἐκείνῳ: read as a characterising phrase (“sorcerers that they are”). θεσπεσίους θυρωρούς rendered “marvellous doorkeepers” (ironic in Celsus’s mouth). ἀνασκολοπίζεσθε: “impaled”, Celsus’s word for execution by stake or cross; kept literal in Origen’s reply too, since he picks up the same verb. τῶν προκατειλεγμένων (of those listed earlier): the other archons named in Book 6. No Scripture quoted. Review: δι᾿ εὐσεβείας ... ὑπερβολήν parsed as διά + accusative ὑπερβολήν with dependent genitive εὐσεβείας (“from an excess of piety”). Celsus’s accusatives (τὴν ... ἀπάτην ... θυρωρούς) have no governing verb in the excerpt; kept as a fragment rather than turned into “Such is”. ἀθλίως / δύστηνοι / κακῶς given distinct renderings.
Reordered the 'sorcerers' clause so 'Jesus and all the worship of God' stay together; 'that comes from him' -> 'that he taught'
Dropped the added 'And so' before Celsus's quotation
Restored 'truly' (ὡς ἀληθῶς): 'more wretched even than what are truly idols'; 'worship' -> 'revere' for σέβοντες
Celsus's accusative fragment no longer recast as 'Such is the deceit'; three distinct words for ἀθλίως / δύστηνοι / κακῶς
Fixed the parse of δι᾿ εὐσεβείας ὑπερβολήν: 'from an excess of piety' (was 'through piety, to excess'); gloss corrected
